claim: The water cycle continuously moves water between oceans atmosphere land and living organisms through evaporation precipitation and runoff
The carbon cycle describes the movement of carbon between the atmosphere biosphere oceans and geosphere
Earthquakes occur when tectonic stress along fault lines exceeds the frictional strength of rocks causing sudden displacement
The Richter scale measures earthquake magnitude logarithmically so each whole number increase represents a tenfold increase in amplitude
Glaciers contain about 69 percent of the world fresh water and their melting contributes significantly to sea level rise
The nitrogen cycle converts atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by living organisms through fixation nitrification and denitrification
Wetlands act as natural water filters absorbing pollutants and excess nutrients while providing habitat for diverse species
Ocean currents are driven by wind temperature and salinity differences distributing heat around the globe and influencing climate
Volcanic eruptions can cool global temperatures by injecting sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere where it forms reflective aerosols
The ozone hole over Antarctica forms each spring due to chlorofluorocarbon-derived chlorine destroying stratospheric ozone
Deforestation contributes approximately 10 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions through loss of carbon storage
Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel their symbiotic algae primarily due to elevated water temperatures
Keystone species have disproportionately large effects on their ecosystem relative to their abundance
Invasive species are non-native organisms that cause ecological or economic harm in their introduced environment
The Amazon rainforest produces approximately 6 percent of the world oxygen and stores an estimated 150 to 200 billion tonnes of carbon
Acid rain forms when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react with water vapor in the atmosphere producing sulfuric and nitric acids
Groundwater provides drinking water for approximately half the world population and supports 40 percent of irrigated agriculture
Mangrove forests protect coastlines from storms sequester carbon and provide nursery habitat for many marine species
Soil takes hundreds to thousands of years to form but can be lost to erosion in a single generation of poor land management
Urban heat islands cause cities to be several degrees warmer than surrounding rural areas due to heat-absorbing surfaces and waste heat
